jvm_option.title: Java did not accept a JVM option
jvm_option.cause: This Java does not understand the JVM option {option}, so the game could not start.
jvm_option.fix: Remove or correct it in the installation's JVM options, or choose a Java that knows it.

heap_unavailable.title: Java could not reserve the memory
heap_unavailable.cause: Java could not set aside {memory, number, ::group-off} MiB for the game. The computer has less free memory than that, or the Java is 32-bit.
heap_unavailable.fix: Lower the installation's memory or close other programs. The launcher's own Java is 64-bit.

java_too_old.title: The game needs a newer Java
java_too_old.cause: {required, select, none {The game or one of its mods needs a newer Java} other {The game or one of its mods needs Java {required}}}{found, select, none {.} other {, but Java {found} started it.}}
java_too_old.fix: Choose the launcher's Java for this installation; it picks the version the game needs. If you chose your own Java, choose a newer one.

java_too_new.title: The game needs an older Java
java_too_new.cause: This Minecraft or mod loader was made for an older Java{found, select, none {} other { and does not run on Java {found}}}. Minecraft 1.16 and older with mod loaders usually needs Java 8.
java_too_new.fix: Choose the launcher's Java for this installation, or your own Java 8.

missing_dependency.title: A mod needs another mod
missing_dependency.cause: {mod} needs {dependency}{required, select, none {} other { ({required})}}, which is not installed.{count, plural, =1 {} other { # requirements are missing in all.}}
missing_dependency.fix: Add {dependency} for this Minecraft version and mod loader to the mods folder, or remove {mod}.

wrong_dependency_version.title: A mod needs another version of a mod
wrong_dependency_version.cause: {mod} needs {dependency}{required, select, none {} other { {required}}}{found, select, none {} other {, but {found} is installed}}.{count, plural, =1 {} other { # requirements are unmet in all.}}
wrong_dependency_version.fix: Update {dependency} in the mods folder to the version {mod} asks for, or use an older {mod}.

wrong_minecraft_version.title: A mod is made for another Minecraft version
wrong_minecraft_version.cause: {mod} needs Minecraft {required}{found, select, none {} other {, but this installation is {found}}}.
wrong_minecraft_version.fix: Download the {mod} file made for this Minecraft version, or remove it.

loader_too_old.title: A mod needs a newer mod loader
loader_too_old.cause: {mod, select, none {A mod} other {{mod}}} needs a newer {dependency, select, none {mod loader} other {{dependency}}}{required, select, none {} other { ({required})}}{found, select, none {} other {; this installation has {found}}}.
loader_too_old.fix: Choose a newer loader version in the installation's settings, or use an older version of the mod.

incompatible_mods.title: Two mods cannot run together
incompatible_mods.fix: Remove one of them from the mods folder.

duplicate_mods.title: A mod is installed twice
duplicate_mods.cause: {modId, select, none {The same mod is installed more than once.} other {The mod {modId} is installed more than once{files, select, none {.} other {: {files}.}}}}
duplicate_mods.fix: Keep only one file of it, the newest, in the mods folder.

mod_for_other_loader.title: A mod is made for another loader
mod_for_other_loader.cause: {file, select, none {Some files in the mods folder are {loader, select, none {made for another loader} other {{loader} mods}}, so this installation's loader skips them.} other {{file} is {loader, select, none {made for another loader} other {a {loader} mod}}, so this installation's loader skips it.}}
mod_for_other_loader.fix: Remove it, or download the version made for this installation's loader.

corrupt_mod_file.title: A file is damaged
corrupt_mod_file.cause: {file, select, none {A game or mod file} other {{file}}} is damaged or incomplete, often after an interrupted download.
corrupt_mod_file.fix: {place, select, mods {Delete it from the mods folder and download it again.} other {Repair the installation to download it again.}}

corrupt_config.title: A config file is damaged
corrupt_config.cause: {file, select, none {A config file} other {The config file {file}}} could not be read: it is damaged or empty, often after the computer shut down while the game was running.
corrupt_config.fix: Delete it from the config folder; the game creates it again with default settings.

mixin_failed.title: A mod could not change the game's code
mixin_failed.cause: {modId, select, none {A mod} other {The mod {modId}}} failed to apply its changes to the game (Mixin). It is usually made for another version of Minecraft or of another mod, or conflicts with another mod.
mixin_failed.fix: Update or remove this mod; its page lists the version for this Minecraft and loader.

mod_failed_to_load.title: A mod failed to start
mod_failed_to_load.cause: {modId, select, none {A mod} other {The mod {modId}}} hit an error while the loader started it.
mod_failed_to_load.fix: Update or remove it. If the crash is new, remove the mods you added last.

optifine_conflict.title: OptiFine does not work here
optifine_conflict.cause: OptiFine does not work with this loader version or with other mods, such as Sodium, Embeddium or Rubidium.
optifine_conflict.fix: Remove OptiFine, or use the OptiFine release made for exactly this Forge version. With Fabric, use Sodium and Iris instead.

out_of_memory.title: The game ran out of memory
out_of_memory.cause: The game used all {memory, number, ::group-off} MiB it was given.
out_of_memory.fix: Give the installation more memory: {suggested, number, ::group-off} MiB is a good start. Many mods, shaders or a long render distance need more.

pack_needs_memory.title: The modpack asks for more memory
pack_needs_memory.cause: {required, select, none {The modpack needs more memory than this installation gives the game.} other {The modpack needs at least {required} MiB, but this installation gives the game {memory} MiB.}}
pack_needs_memory.fix: {required, select, none {Give the installation more memory in its settings, then start again.} other {Give the installation at least {required} MiB in its settings, then start again.}}

system_memory.title: The computer ran out of memory
system_memory.cause: Java could not get memory from the system. Other programs use the rest, or the {memory, number, ::group-off} MiB given to the game leave too little for everything else.
system_memory.fix: Close other programs or lower the installation's memory. On Windows a larger paging file also helps.

killed.title: The game was killed
killed.cause: The system or another program ended the game at once. On Linux this is usually the out-of-memory killer, when the computer runs out of memory.
killed.fix: Close other programs or lower the installation's memory, then start again.

opengl_unsupported.title: The graphics driver offers no suitable OpenGL
opengl_unsupported.cause: The game could not open its window because the graphics driver does not offer the OpenGL version Minecraft needs{error, select, none {} other { (GLFW error {error})}}.
opengl_unsupported.fix: Install the newest driver from the graphics card's maker (AMD, Intel or NVIDIA), not the one Windows chose. On a laptop, run Java on the dedicated graphics card.

graphics_driver.title: The graphics driver crashed
graphics_driver.cause: The game crashed inside the {vendor, select, amd {AMD} intel {Intel} nvidia {NVIDIA} mesa {Mesa} other {graphics}} driver ({module}).
graphics_driver.fix: Update or reinstall the graphics driver from the maker's site. Shaders and overlays can set it off too: try without them.

overlay.title: An overlay crashed the game
overlay.cause: {program, select, none {A program that draws over games} other {{program}, a program that draws over games,}} crashed the game.
overlay.fix: Turn off overlays and recorders (RivaTuner or MSI Afterburner, the Discord overlay, OBS game capture, D3DGear, the NVIDIA overlay) and start again.

native_crash.title: The game crashed outside Java
native_crash.cause: The game crashed in native code{module, select, none {} other { ({module})}}{signal, select, none {} other {, {signal}}}. Graphics drivers, overlays, antivirus software or a damaged Java are the usual causes.
native_crash.fix: Update the graphics driver, turn off overlays and repair the installation. The JVM error file (hs_err) in the game folder has the details.

missing_native_library.title: A game library is missing
missing_native_library.cause: The game could not load its native library{library, select, none {} other { {library}}}.
missing_native_library.fix: Repair the installation to download it again. Antivirus software sometimes removes these files.

broken_installation.title: Game files are incomplete
broken_installation.cause: Files the game or Java needs are missing or damaged.

disk_full.title: The disk is full
disk_full.cause: The game could not write a file because the disk has no free space.
disk_full.fix: Free space on the disk that holds the launcher's data, then start again.

file_access.title: A file could not be used
file_access.cause: {file, select, none {A file} other {The file {file}}} is locked by another program or may not be read or written.
file_access.fix: Close programs that may use it (another copy of the game, a backup or sync program, antivirus software) and start again.

world_load_failed.title: The world could not be loaded
world_load_failed.cause: The game failed while reading a world ({description}).
world_load_failed.fix: Restore the world from a backup. If a mod was removed or updated, put back the version the world was made with.

ticking_entity.title: An entity crashes the world
ticking_entity.cause: {entity, select, none {An entity} other {The entity {entity}}}{position, select, none {} other { at {position}}} crashes the game every time it updates.
ticking_entity.fix: Restore the world from a backup, or update or remove the mod that adds this entity.

ticking_block_entity.title: A block crashes the world
ticking_block_entity.cause: {block, select, none {A block} other {The block {block}}}{position, select, none {} other { at {position}}} crashes the game every time it updates.
ticking_block_entity.fix: Restore the world from a backup, or update or remove the mod that adds this block.

server_hang.title: The game froze
server_hang.cause: The game stopped responding{seconds, select, none {} other { for {seconds} seconds}} and its watchdog ended it. Large builds, many mods or too little memory cause this.
server_hang.fix: Give the game more memory and update or remove the mods named in the crash report. If one world causes it, restore it from a backup.

debug_crash.title: Crash by F3 + C
debug_crash.cause: The crash was started on purpose by holding F3 + C.
debug_crash.fix: Nothing is broken. Holding F3 + C for ten seconds crashes the game to test it.

game_crash.title: The game crashed
game_crash.cause: The game wrote a crash report: “{description}”{exception, select, none {.} other {: {exception}}}
game_crash.fix: Open the crash report for details. If mods are named here, update or remove them first.

terminated.title: Another program ended the game
terminated.cause: Another program asked the game to stop; it was not the launcher's Stop button.
terminated.fix: If it was not you, look for a program that ends other programs, then start again.

console_question.title: The game waited for an answer it could not get
console_question.cause: The game asked a question in a console window, which the launcher cannot show, and kept asking. The launcher ended it.
console_question.fix: Read the lines below: they usually name the problem, such as a damaged file or too little memory. Fix it and start again.

unknown.title: The game exited with an error
unknown.cause: {exitCode, select, none {The game stopped} other {The game exited with code {exitCode}}} and printed no cause the launcher knows.
unknown.fix: Look at the output below and the crash reports. If it started after a change, undo it: remove the mods or options you added last.
